taxonomyNote: Domesticated form of the European polecat; Animal Diversity Web, CDFW and the Global Invasive Species Database also write it M. putorius furo, and note unresolved taxonomy.
fieldMarks: Long slender body; adults 33-41 cm plus tail (males larger, 0.9-2.7 kg; females 0.3-1.1 kg)
Three basic colour forms: dark polecat-type, sandy/pastel with brownish guard hairs, or all white; feral populations tend toward the wild polecat colour
Five non-retractable claws on each paw; 34 teeth
behavior: Crepuscular; sleeps 18-20 hours a day as a pet
Obligate carnivore of small prey; in New Zealand feral ferrets rely mainly on rabbits
Dens in rabbit holes, scrub, buildings and haystacks
Wild ferrets live about two to four years
habitat: In New Zealand: grasslands, scrub, pasture, riverbeds, forest fringes and urban edges.
range: Domestic worldwide. The sources read document feral populations mainly outside North America (New Zealand, islands); CDFW discusses escapes and case studies in the US but does not describe an established North American feral population.

lookalikes.name: Black-footed ferret
lookalikes.howToTell: A different, native North American species (Mustela nigripes); not a feral domestic ferret.
